title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'équation des lacets' notes Grothendieck solves an adelic, linear model of the loop equations inside GL(2, Ẑ). The unknowns are alpha_0 = (a b; c d) with det = eps_3 = ±1, and f = (r s; t u) in SL(2, Ẑ). They must satisfy alpha_0 rho(alpha_0)^{-1} = eps_2 l_0^gamma (f sigma_inf ...)^{-1}, where sigma_inf is the order-4 element, rho relates to the order-3 element, l_0 = (1 1; 0 1), and mu = 2 gamma + 1 is the 'multiplier'.

Previous page (85)-(87): solutions exist iff c^2 + cd + d^2 = ±(t^2 + u^2) in Ẑ*. Then 1/mu = eps_2(t^2 + u^2) = eps_3(c^2 + cd + d^2), with eps_2 ≡ mu mod 4 and eps_3 ≡ mu mod 3. This is the local fact that a unit of Ẑ is a norm from Z[i] (resp. Z[omega]) exactly up to the sign obstruction at 2 (resp. 3).

This page gives the parametrisation of all solutions.
(i) Choose (eps_2, eps_3, mu), two choices up to the global sign.
(ii) Choose r, s with ur - ts = 1. Such r, s exist because t^2 + u^2 is a unit, so for every prime p the components t_p, u_p are not both in pZ_p. Hence (t, u) is a unimodular vector of Ẑ^2. The solutions form an affine Ẑ-line (r, s) = (r_0 + lambda t, s_0 + lambda u).
(iii) A crossed-out computation follows. Put f · tf = (R S; S U) with R = r^2 + s^2, S = rt + su, U = t^2 + u^2; this matrix equals f sigma_inf f^{-1} sigma_inf^{-1} for f in SL2. He then defines successively D = 1/mu = eps_2 U, C = eps_2 S, B = C + D - 1, A = (1 + BC)/D. This yields (A B; C D) in SL2 with C + D - B = 1, D a unit, and the relation (A + 2nu C, B + 2nu D; C, D) = eps_2 (R S; T U), which he says reduces to the corner relation A + 2nu C = eps_2 R.

Verification: B + 2nu D = eps_2 S iff D(1 + 2nu) = 1, i.e. nu = gamma. Then A + 2nu C = (1 + C(B + 2nu D))/D = (1 + S^2)/(eps_2 U) = eps_2 R, because RU - S^2 = det(f · tf) = 1. So the relation is automatic, which plausibly explains why the passage was struck out.

Next page: a, b are found uniquely from a linear system whose determinant is c^2 + cd + d^2, a unit. The solution scheme is thus fibred as follows: mu, then the conic (t, u), then the conic (c, d), then lambda in Ẑ, then (a, b) unique. This matches the 'smooth of relative dimension 4' claim on p.380.

Purpose: an explicit description of the 'linear' (congruence / GL2(Ẑ)) shadow of the loop-equation solutions, i.e. of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type pairs (mu = 2m + 1, f) projected to SL2(Ẑ).
errors: Previous page (86) writes c^2+cd+u^2; this should be c^2+cd+d^2 (a slip).
The next page writes mu ≡ eps_2 (2); this should be mod 4, as in (87) of p.380, since mod 2 is vacuous for units.
Equation label (87) is reused on this page for the parametrisation of (r,s), duplicating (87) of the previous page; (88) is likewise reused on the next page.
The crossed-out derivation is correct; the 'relation (57)' it checks is automatic, since RU - S^2 = 1, so no real gap.

ideas.what: A unit mu of Ẑ is represented by x^2+y^2 up to sign eps_2 ≡ mu mod 4, and by x^2+xy+y^2 up to sign eps_3 ≡ mu mod 3. This links the order-4 and order-3 elements of SL2 to the norm forms of Z[i] and Z[omega].
ideas.modern_name: Local representation of units by binary norm forms; conjugacy of elliptic elements of SL2 over Z_p via Z[i], Z[omega] (Latimer–MacDuffee type)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Gauss; Latimer–MacDuffee for the matrix–ideal correspondence)

ideas.what: Completing a unimodular row (t,u) of Ẑ^2 to an SL2(Ẑ) matrix, with the solution set an affine line (r_0,s_0) + lambda(t,u).
ideas.modern_name: Unimodular row completion / torsor under the unipotent stabilizer

ideas.what: Explicit parametrisation of solutions of the adelic linearised loop equation in GL2(Ẑ) by (mu, (t,u), (c,d), lambda), giving a smooth scheme of relative dimension 4.
ideas.modern_name: Image/analogue of GT-type equations in the congruence quotient SL2(Ẑ); multiplier = cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT side: Drinfeld 1990, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps; this explicit SL2(Ẑ) parametrisation is not standard in print
ideas.where_published: Possibly related themes in La Longue Marche (1981); unsure about this computation

missed.claim: An explicit, elementary parametrisation of the solution set of the linearised (congruence-level, adelic) loop equations. Simultaneous representability of 1/mu by the Gaussian and Eisenstein norm forms controls the signs eps_2, eps_3. This is a complete small computation, but its content is classical; at most it documents how Grothendieck tested the loop equations at the SL2(Ẑ) level.
missed.quote: et si r_0, s_0 est une solution, les autres s'obtiennent sous forme paramétrique (r,s) = (r_0 + λt, s_0 + λu)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginally: it is a sanity-check model of GT-type equations projected to SL2(Ẑ), which is of interest for historians of the Longue Marche. It contains no new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine linear algebra over Ẑ completing a parametrisation; the arithmetic input (local norm-form representability) is classical, and the struck-out check is automatically satisfied.
transcription_corrections: 'car r^2 ε u^2 ∈ Ẑ*' should read 'car t^2 + u^2 ∈ Ẑ*'.
'μ_x' is most likely just 'μ' (the multiplier); the subscript is a pen artefact or unclear.
The crossed-out passage begins at 'on en déduit'; the expression transcribed 'f∘(f*)^{-1}' is likely f σ_∞ f^{-1} σ_∞^{-1} (or similar), equal to f · tf for f in SL2.
In (88) the first line reads D = 1/μ = ε_3(c^2+cd+d^2) = ε_2(t^2+u^2) = ε_2 U, with a scribbled correction toward ε_2 U at the end.
The whole lower half of the page (from 'Ayant choisi r, s' to the end) is struck through with large diagonal crosses.
